title: French Fries
description:
Serves 3 to 4. Published July 1, 2009. From Cook's Illustrated.
Flavoring the oil with bacon fat (optional) gives the fries a mild meaty flavor. We prefer peanut oil for frying, but vegetable or canola oil can be substituted. This recipe will not work with sweet potatoes or russets. Our easier approach to cooking French fries does not preheat the oil and calls for one prolonged frying of Yukon Gold potatoes (result is one third less fat in the fried).
ingredients: 2 1/2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes (about 6 medium), scrubbed, dried, sides squared off, and cut lengthwise into 1/4-inch by 1/4-inch batons (see note)
directions: Combine potatoes, oil (at room temperature), and bacon fat (if using) in large Dutch oven. Cook over high heat until oil has reached rolling boil, about 5 minutes. Continue to cook, without stirring, until potatoes are limp but exteriors are beginning to firm, about 15 minutes.

Using tongs, stir potatoes, gently scraping up any that stick, and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and crisp, 5 to 10 minutes longer. Using skimmer or slotted spoon, transfer fries to thick paper bag or paper towels. Season with salt and serve immediately.
Whisk together the following for a ½ cup of dressing.
Square off potato by cutting a 1/4-inch-thick slice from each of its 4 long sides.
Stack 3 to 4 planks and cut into 1/4-inch batons. Repeat with remaining planks.
